definition: Java Data Mining (JDM) is a standard Java API for developing data mining applications and tools.
details: JDM defines an object model and Java API for data mining objects and processes. JDM enables applications to integrate data mining technology for developing predictive analytics applications and tools. The JDM 1.0 standard was developed under the Java Community Process as JSR 73. In 2006, the JDM 2.0 specification was being developed under JSR 247, but has been withdrawn in 2011 without standardization. Various data mining functions and techniques like statistical classification and association, regression analysis, data clustering, and attribute importance are covered by the 1.0 release of this standard. It never received wide acceptance, and there is no known implementation.

explainer.lead: Java Data Mining (JDM) is a standard Java API for developing data mining applications and tools, letting applications integrate data mining technology for predictive analytics. It matters as an attempt to make mining models portable across Java tools through a common object model.

tiers.eli5: It's a shared plug shape so different data-mining programs and tools can connect to a Java application without custom wiring each time.
tiers.practitioner: Developers code against the JDM object model and API so an application can use data mining functions such as statistical classification and association. The pitfall is assuming full standardization: the 2.0 effort was withdrawn in 2011, so only the 1.0 standard was completed.
tiers.paperLevel: JDM defines an object model and Java API for data mining objects and processes; version 1.0 was developed under the Java Community Process as JSR 73, while 2.0 (JSR 247) was withdrawn in 2011 without standardization. Known limits: standardization stopped at 1.0.

explainer.example: A Java application invokes a JDM classification function through the standard API, keeping its predictive analytics code independent of a particular mining tool.
